exposureType: Gulf War Illness / Chronic Multisymptom Illness
description: Medically unexplained chronic multisymptom illness affecting Gulf War veterans
eligibleLocations: Neutral Zone between Iraq and Saudi Arabia

servicePeriod.description: Ongoing as the Gulf War period never officially ended

qualifyingSymptoms.description: Must have one or more of these medically unexplained chronic symptoms that appeared during or after Gulf War service

manifestations: Extreme tiredness not improved by rest

presumptiveConditions.description: Severe chronic fatigue lasting 6 months or more
Widespread musculoskeletal pain with tenderness in localized areas
Chronic functional gastrointestinal disorders including IBS, functional dyspepsia, functional abdominal pain syndrome
Chronic multisymptom illness of unknown etiology presenting with multiple symptoms
presumptiveConditions.note: Must have multiple symptoms from at least two of the qualifying categories

presumptiveConditions.description: Medically unexplained symptoms that may include but are not limited to fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, cognitive problems
presumptiveConditions.note: Does not require a specific diagnosis - symptoms alone can qualify

evidenceRequirements.serviceConnection: Presumptive - Must have served in Southwest Asia theater during Gulf War period
evidenceRequirements.medicalEvidence: Current diagnosis or documented chronic symptoms (6+ months)
evidenceRequirements.layEvidence: Helpful but not required - buddy statements can support symptom onset
evidenceRequirements.disabilityRating: Must be at least 10% disabling to qualify for presumptive service connection

specialConsiderations.multipleSymptoms: Veterans often have multiple qualifying symptoms - each should be evaluated separately
specialConsiderations.chronicRequirement: Symptoms must be chronic (6+ months) to qualify
specialConsiderations.noSpecificDiagnosis: Undiagnosed illness provision allows service connection without specific medical diagnosis
specialConsiderations.timeLimit: Most conditions have no time limit for manifestation - can appear years after service

references: M21-1, Part IV, Subpart ii, Chapter 2, Section D
VA Gulf War Veterans Illnesses Biomedical Research
